A_note: Cochrane named as an example of a place people move to.

A_note: Supports the interim Banff-Jasper riding and says the areas removed from Banff-Kananaskis are "basically suburbs of either Cochrane or Calgary" and "fit well with the new ridings that you put them in". A_note: MLA for Calgary-Bow wants Springbank moved from the interim Cochrane-Springbank into Calgary-Bow. Speaks to Springbank's placement, not to who Cochrane should be with; coded like the Beiseker case (rule 8). A reader could record rejects=C1 for the Springbank part.

B_quote: These conclusions are sound and the Commission should apply consistent logic to Springbank and Calgary-Bow. Springbank is more connected to Calgary than Cochrane.

B_quote: the residents of Springbank would be far better served by being included within the Calgary Bow electoral district rather than being aligned with Cochrane or Canmore

B_note: Canmore writer wants Springbank moved to Calgary-Bow and a Canmore-Rocky Mountain Corridor district. Accepts Cochrane-Springbank otherwise ('slight tweaks to Cochrane-Springbank's east', p. 20), so rejects=C1 is partial (Springbank component only).
B_quote: Placing Springbank in Cochrane-Springbank severs these bonds, grouping it with more remote, horse-country communities north toward Cochrane

A_note: Form header: about "58 - Cochrane-Springbank". Springbank resident wants Springbank in a Calgary district; Cochrane is not named in the message.
B_note: Header: about '58 - Cochrane-Springbank'; Cochrane named only there. Springbank resident wants Springbank in a Calgary district rather than the interim riding. Nothing on Cochrane's other partners.
B_quote: it seems this would be the perfect opportunity for the area we live in to be swept into the adjoining City of Calgary electoral district(s)

A_note: West Springs resident wanting Springbank in Calgary-Bow; says Springbank is not "a satellite of Cochrane". About Springbank's placement (rule 8). A reader could record rejects=C1 for the Springbank part.
A_quote: forcing them into a riding with distant rural hamlets like Madden only serves to disconnect them from their primary service hub in West Calgary.

A_note: Springbank resident wanting Calgary-Bow. About Springbank's placement (rule 8). A reader could record rejects=C1 for the Springbank part.
A_quote: While the commission has proposed a new Cochrane-Springbank constituency, this grouping fundamentally ignores the reality of where Springbank residents live their lives.
B_note: Springbank resident; wants Springbank in Calgary-Bow; 'Grouping us with them dilutes our voice'. rejects=C1 is partial (Springbank component only).
B_quote: While the commission has proposed a new Cochrane-Springbank constituency, this grouping fundamentally ignores the reality of where Springbank residents live their lives.

A_note: Local historian; offers history as 'why we are a little different than the rural areas around us' and defends 13th Street as the East/West divider. No explicit request; precedent offered in support of the status quo. A second reader could fairly code mentions=1, no want.

B_note: Local historian giving history: 'we have had a riding that has only been urban since 1909. We have never included rural areas since 1909, a long precedence for our community' and 13th Street as a natural east-west divider. Leans to L1 but is offered as context, with no request in the (abridged) record; rule 17, narrower code.

A_note: Bellevue (Livingstone-Macleod) resident. Rejects rural area being joined to Lethbridge; no stated want for how the city itself is divided (implied L1). Chair summarises "you do not want to be lumped in with Lethbridge". Rejects-only row: majority code not defined by section 5, set to 1.
A_quote: The softening of that language makes me concerned as a rural person because the idea of being subsumed by Lethbridge is horrifying.
B_note: Rural Livingstone-Macleod resident (Bellevue); round 1, reacting to talk of blended ridings. Does not say how the city itself should be divided; her wish is that her rural riding not be joined to Lethbridge, which implies the city stays apart (L1 at direction). Chair later summarises 'you do not want to be lumped in with Lethbridge'; she does not dispute it.
B_quote: The softening of that language makes me concerned as a rural person because the idea of being subsumed by Lethbridge is horrifying.

A_note: Lethbridge resident; argues against the anticipated wedge/hybrid design ("Costco version of redistricting") from the rural side. No explicit want; implied L1. Rejects-only: majority code set to 1.
A_quote: let’s take a portion of Lethbridge and put a big wedge of the rest of southern Alberta […] you have to resist the temptation to turn those ridings into a mixed riding.
B_note: Lethbridge resident. Argues against joining portions of Lethbridge to rural southern Alberta ('you have to resist the temptation to turn those ridings into a mixed riding'); asked by Chair 'are you for or against blended ridings?' answers 'I'm against them. They don't work.' No EB label precedes the quote.
B_quote: let’s take a portion of Lethbridge and put a big wedge of the rest of southern Alberta, and it will all come down to Lethbridge, and it’ll make the numbers, and it’ll look really good. Well, that’s what I call the Costco version of redistricting.

A_note: High River resident: Livingstone-Macleod should not extend toward Lethbridge. Rejects rural-city joining from the rural side (rule 8); no want on how the city is divided. Rejects-only: majority code set to 1.
A_quote: interests there as part of a much larger city differ significantly from those of our rural riding, and I would be very much against extending in that direction
B_note: High River resident writing about Livingstone-Macleod. Speaks for the rural riding: it should not be extended toward Lethbridge. Says nothing of how the city itself is divided, so L1 only at direction (city and country kept apart). A stricter reader could leave want blank and record the rejection only.
B_quote: There is a somewhat natural economic corridor toward Lethbridge, but interests there as part of a much larger city differ significantly from those of our rural riding, and I would be very much against extending in that direction.

A_note: Objects to the internal east-west line only (wants Lethbridge-West confined west of the Oldman). Silent on city-country joining, so no want on this element; a reader could put L9.
A_quote: it would be entirely inappropriate to extend the boundary of the West Lethbridge electoral district across the river
B_note: Lethbridge-West resident. Objects to the interim line BETWEEN the two city ridings and wants the Oldman River as the divide; says nothing about joining city and country. Coded L1 at direction because the request presupposes two ridings inside the city; a stricter reader would code mention with no want. Hard case.
B_quote: it would be entirely inappropriate to extend the boundary of the West Lethbridge electoral district across the river

A_note: Argues against four districts with rural communities added (wording muddled: "adding them to city centres would be invaluable"). No stated want; implied L1. Rejects-only: majority code set to 1.
A_quote: The proposed changes to turn the Lethbridge riding from 2 to 4 districts would not benefit the province.
B_note: Lethbridge-West resident. Treats the four-district idea as a live proposal (it is not on the interim map). Opposes going from two to four and adding rural communities to 'city centres' ('would be invaluable' reads as 'of no value' in context). Keeping two city ridings is implied, not stated: direction.
B_quote: The proposed changes to turn the Lethbridge riding from 2 to 4 districts would not benefit the province.

A_note: Edmonton writer who believes Lethbridge is proposed to be paired with rural areas (the interim map did not). Rejects-only: majority code set to 1.
A_quote: our urban centres in Edmonton and Lethbridge that have been proposed to be paired up in ways that just don't make sense. I urge you, do not go through with this!
B_note: Edmonton resident. Believes Lethbridge has been proposed for pairing with rural areas (the interim map did not do so); 'I do not believe it makes sense to split up urban centres and pair them up with rural ones'. Want inferred from the rejection: direction.
B_quote: our urban centres in Edmonton and Lethbridge that have been proposed to be paired up in ways that just don't make sense. I urge you, do not go through with this!

A_note: Rejection only; implied L1. Rejects-only: majority code set to 1.
A_quote: I am not in favour of the changes to make lethbridge split into four areas expanding into rural surrounding areas.
B_note: Lethbridge-East resident. Treats the four-way split as pending. Keeping the city ridings is implied by the rejection, not stated: direction.
B_quote: I am not in favour of the changes to make lethbridge split into four areas expanding into rural surrounding areas.

A_note: Rejection only; implied L1. Rejects-only: majority code set to 1.
A_quote: Do not split Lethbridge into 4 districts. This will weaken Lethbridge and not accurately represent our needs.
B_note: Lethbridge-East resident. Whole message. Keeping the two city ridings is implied, not stated: direction.
B_quote: Do not split Lethbridge into 4 districts. This will weaken Lethbridge and not accurately represent our needs.

A_note: Place from header (rule 2): Lethbridge, about "70 - Lethbridge-West". "The proposal" she finds abhorrent is adding rural areas to urban ridings, which the interim map did not do. Rejects-only: majority code set to 1.
A_quote: I suspect it be an attempt to silence the more progressive voting areas by including more rural in urban ridings.
B_note: Message names no place; form header gives Lethbridge, AB and '70 - Lethbridge-West' (rule 2). 'The proposal' she finds 'abhorrent' is adding rural areas to urban ridings, which the interim map did not do in Lethbridge; read as the four-way hybrid idea. Want inferred from the rejection. B_quote: I suspect it be an attempt to silence the more progressive voting areas by including more rural in urban ridings.

A_note: Rejection only; implied L1. Calls the four-way split "the current proposal" though the interim map did not adopt it. Rejects-only: majority code set to 1.
A_quote: The current proposal to split the two Lethbridge ridings into four ridings that meld urban and rural constituencies will serve neither well.
B_note: Lethbridge-West resident. Treats the four-way split as the 'current proposal' (it is not on the interim map). Keeping two city ridings is implied by the rejection: direction.
B_quote: The current proposal to split the two Lethbridge ridings into four ridings that meld urban and rural constituencies will serve neither well.

A_note: Place from header: Lethbridge, about Lethbridge-West. General statement that urban and rural needs differ; read as against splitting the city into mixed ridings. Rejects-only: majority code set to 1.
A_quote: Splitting up urban dilutes this for good representation.
B_note: Message names no place; form header gives Lethbridge and '70 - Lethbridge-West' (rule 2). Argues against splitting up the urban riding and mixing it with rural needs; want inferred from that. A stricter reader could treat it as HYBRID-GENERAL only.
B_quote: I believe that urban electoral needs/concerns are quite different from rural needs. Splitting up urban dilutes this for good representation.

A_note: High River; Livingstone-Macleod should not extend toward Lethbridge ("that city’s urban and surrounding interests differ markedly from those of our rural communities"). Same person and point as EBC-2025-1-0061. Rejects-only: majority code set to 1.
A_quote: I am strongly opposed to extending the boundary in that direction
B_note: High River resident (same person as EBC-2025-1-0061) defending the north-south Livingstone-Macleod against the interim east-west ridings. Rural side of the question: his riding should not reach toward Lethbridge. Says nothing of how the city is divided, so L1 only at direction.
B_quote: while there is a natural economic link toward Lethbridge, the impact of that city’s urban and surrounding interests differ markedly from those of our rural communities, and I am strongly opposed to extending the boundary in that direction

A_note: Rocky Mountain House area resident. B_note: Rocky Mountain House area resident. Asks to keep the Rimbey-Rocky Mountain House-Sundre riding and build along Highways 11 and 22; that keeps Sundre with the foothills riding, but he never speaks of Sundre or the Olds riding apart from the riding's name, hence direction. Fallback: Sylvan Lake a better partner than Lacombe. Quote precedes the first EB label; page is the record's PDF range.
B_quote: please use the full range of population possibilities from 41,198 to consider the status quo with respect to the boundaries in Rimbey-Rocky Mountain House-Sundre.

Endorses the interim Airdrie-East and Airdrie-West as drawn and counts Crossfield and Irricana as part of the Airdrie-East area (rule 5: support for an interim arrangement is a want for it; 'Crossfield belongs with Airdrie' = O2). B_quote: We're here today to just let you know that we are very supportive of the proposed ridings in the report.

A_note: Wild Rose School Division trustee. Asks that the current boundaries affecting Clearwater County remain and, to the Chair, confirms a return to Rimbey-Rocky Mountain House-Sundre. Stance belongs under RMH-A.
B_note: Wild Rose School Division trustee. Asks to keep the current boundaries and, when the Chair asks whether she wants 'a return to the Rimbey-Rocky Mountain House-Sundre riding', answers 'The Rimbey-Rocky Mountain House-Sundre. Yeah.' (EB-654; audio was breaking up). Keeping that riding keeps Sundre out of the Olds riding, but she speaks only of Clearwater County, never of Sundre or Mountain View; direction, low confidence. A narrower reading is mention only. Quote precedes the first EB label.
B_quote: We are here to respectfully request that the current electoral boundaries affecting Clearwater county remain as they are.

A_note: MLA for West Yellowhead; his request is to keep Jasper with Hinton and Grande Cache (J1). Mention without want (rule 17). quote_react precedes the first EB label.
B_note: MLA for West Yellowhead; his request is to keep Jasper with Hinton (J1). In passing he endorses a central mountain region of 'Banff, Rocky Mountain House, Sundre' and says holding the regions together 'is critical for the effective representation of the people in all three regions', which places Sundre with the foothills riding and not the Olds riding. Direction only, low confidence; a narrower reading is mention only. Record has no EB label before the quote.
B_quote: There are three distinct regions along the mountains: Jasper and Hinton; Banff, Rocky Mountain House, Sundre; and Canmore, Kananaskis.

A_note: Eckville resident, about the interim map as a whole. Approves the break-up of Rimbey-Rocky Mountain House-Sundre (W3 under RMH-A) and the interim boundaries generally. B_note: Eckville resident; header: current 80 - Rimbey-Rocky Mountain House-Sundre, about the boundaries as a whole. Approves the interim map's break-up of the riding, which is what put Sundre into Mountain View-Kneehill (rule 5: support for an interim arrangement). She does not speak of Sundre's placement as such, hence direction and low confidence; a narrower reading is mention only.
B_quote: I love that you broke up Rimbey Rocky Sundre . Very happy with the boundaries.

A_note: Clearwater County resident (codebook worked example 2). Names Mountain View-Kneehill as one of three ridings dividing Clearwater County and objects to eliminating Rimbey-Rocky Mountain House-Sundre; asks that Clearwater County stay whole 'with other west central communities' (W1 under RMH-A). B_note: Clearwater County (Condor) resident; subject line names Mountain View-Kneehill as one of the three divisions. A narrower reading is mention only.
B_quote: keep all communities in Clearwater County in the same riding with other west central communities.

A_note: Wild Rose School Division board. Names Mountain View-Kneehill as one of three ridings dividing Clearwater County; asks for Clearwater County in one constituency aligned 'with other western communities'. No request about Sundre, Mountain View County or the Olds riding.
B_note: Chair, Wild Rose School Division. Main request is Clearwater County whole (W0). Adds that it should be aligned 'with other western communities' and notes families 'north and south of Rocky Mountain House along the Highway 22 corridor'; names Mountain View-Kneehill only as one of the three interim ridings. Sundre and Mountain View County are not named: direction, low confidence; a narrower reading is mention only.
B_quote: a better option would be to keep Clearwater County in a single constituency and align it with other western communities.

A_note: Mayor of Rocky Mountain House. Asks that the town be with all of Clearwater County and keep 'a connection with other communities along the Eastern Slopes region'. Sundre appears only in the name of a tourism development zone that he says the interim map divides among several MLAs; that leans the O1 way but is not a request about Sundre or the Olds riding. Mention without want (rule 17).
B_note: Mayor of Rocky Mountain House. Main request is the town with all of Clearwater County (W0/W1). Asks also for a link to other Eastern Slopes communities and cites the 'Rocky Mountain House-Sundre-Cochrane' tourism zone (p. 84), the only mention of Sundre. No request that names Sundre's riding or the Olds riding: direction, low confidence; a narrower reading is mention only.
B_quote: Rocky Mountain will have the best representation by being located in the same constituency as all of Clearwater County and maintaining a connection with other communities along the Eastern Slopes region.

A_note: Innisfail resident, about 86 - Sylvan Lake-Innisfail. Wants Sylvan Lake moved to Lacombe-Ponoka and, if more population is needed, 'perhaps' Blackfalds or Olds added to the Innisfail riding. Taking Olds out of its own riding would be O9, but the suggestion is conditional and offered as one of two alternatives; left as mention without want (rule 17).
B_note: Innisfail resident; about 86 - Sylvan Lake-Innisfail. Tentative, conditional suggestion that Olds (or Blackfalds) could join the Innisfail riding in place of Sylvan Lake. Olds leaving its own riding is on no map: O9. Because it is offered as 'perhaps', a narrower reading is mention only.

A_note: Former Reeve of Clearwater County. Header names Mountain View-Kneehill among the three ridings. Asks that Clearwater County stay whole 'alongside other west central Alberta communities'; objecting to the elimination of Rimbey-Rocky Mountain House-Sundre implies Sundre stays west (O1), but he says nothing of Sundre itself or the Olds riding: mention without want (rules 1, 17).
B_note: Former Reeve of Clearwater County. Objects to losing the Rimbey-Rocky Mountain House-Sundre riding and asks for Clearwater County whole 'alongside other west central Alberta communities', distinguished from 'prairie and urban communities to the east'. Sundre and Mountain View County are not named outside the riding names: direction, low confidence; a narrower reading is mention only. Close in wording to EBC-2025-2-0409.
B_quote: keep Clearwater County together within a single constituency alongside other west central Alberta communities.

A_note: Airdrie resident, about 51 - Airdrie-East. Wants Airdrie's two districts drawn without the surrounding rural area and small towns (A3 under AIRDRIE). He names Irricana and Beiseker only as places whose needs differ from Airdrie's; by implication they would go to a rural riding (the O1 direction), but he does not say where they belong and never mentions the Olds riding. Mention without want or rejection (rule 17); a reader could fairly record a rejection of the Airdrie-East half of O2.
B_note: Airdrie resident; header: about 51 - Airdrie-East. Wants two Airdrie districts 'without the inclusion of large rural areas' (A3 under AIRDRIE) and argues against Irricana and Beiseker sharing Airdrie-East. He does not say where those villages should go, so the O1 want is by inference from the rejection (rule 4): direction, low confidence. A narrower reading is mention only with the rejection noted.
B_quote: This map is not in the best interest of the residents in Airdrie, who have different needs when compared to Irricana, or Beiseker.

A_note: Mayor for Red Deer County (see his hearing appearance HANSARD-R2-T38-007, where he is more specific and is coded O1 at direction level). This letter objects to the removal of Rimbey-Rocky Mountain House-Sundre and asks that the county keep two divisions; Sundre appears only in the riding name and nothing is said about the Olds/Mountain View riding. Mention without want (rules 1, 17).
B_note: Mayor, for Red Deer County (same person as HANSARD-R2-T38-007). Objects to the loss of the Rimbey-Rocky Mountain House-Sundre riding and wants the county to keep two divisions. Sundre is named only in the riding's name; at the hearing he asked for the riding back 'in some form'. Direction, low confidence; a narrower reading is mention only.
B_quote: The removal of the Rimbey - Rocky Mountain House - Sundre electoral division dilutes the voice of our agricultural community, in particular the ranch style agricultural operations in this environment.

A_note: Lethbridge resident; a 30-page province-wide set of alternative boundaries with 23 figures (pp. 80-109, all read). He thereby leaves the interim riding standing, which could be read as acquiescence in O2, but he says nothing for or against Sundre, Mountain View County, Crossfield, Irricana or Beiseker being where the interim map put them. B_note: Lethbridge resident reviewing the whole interim map. Coded as acceptance of the interim riding in kind (rule 5), direction, low confidence: he never discusses Sundre, Crossfield, Irricana or Beiseker, and the piece of Clearwater County he adjusts is on neither final map. A narrower reading is mention only.
B_quote: This one concerns Banff-Jasper and Mountain View-Kneehill and should not affect a significant number of people. I just don't like the way that the Clearwater River leaves and re-enters the riding.
